items.title: Rebuild Missing Files: show a mod as Ignored (grey, reference-only) if Vortex has it marked Ignored
items.why: A mod deliberately marked Ignored in Vortex currently shows up as an indistinguishable 'Missing' row -- director wants it called out as its own informational status instead, matching the app's existing acknowledged/soft severity tier.
items.prompt:
Real gap: Rebuild Missing Files' scan doesn't know whether Vortex has a mod marked Ignored -- a mod the director deliberately excluded still shows up as a normal 'Missing' row, indistinguishable from a real problem. Director's ask: if a mod involved in a missing-file row is Ignored in Vortex, show it as its own distinct 'Ignored' (grey) status, reference-only -- not something to fix.

REUSE, DON'T REINVENT:
1. **Ignored-mod data**: `lib/sync-runner.js`'s `listIgnoredMods({ stateDir, modId })` -- already exists, already used by Update Collection's own Apply Ignores flow. Scoped per collectionModId (reads that collection's own `rules`, filters `ignored === true`) -- call it once per collection being scanned, same shape as this scan already iterates.
2. **Identity matching**: `lib/vortex-sync/lib.js`'s `identityKeys(x)` -- the ALREADY-ESTABLISHED cross-shape matcher this codebase uses everywhere an Ignored/Disabled ref (`{fileMD5, tag, modId, fileId}`) needs to be matched against a collection.json mod's own `source` shape (`{md5, tag, modId, fileId}`) -- priority fileMD5 > tag > modId+fileId. Use this directly to match a scanned row's `mod.source` against the ignored-refs list -- don't write new matching logic, this exact cross-shape problem is already solved here.
3. **Visual treatment**: this app's already-established 'acknowledged/soft' severity tier (`.mm-row--soft` in Missing Masters, `--neutral`/`--neutral-bg` tokens, documented in DESIGN.md) -- grey, muted, action buttons suppressed, informational only. Reuse this exact tier/token pair for an 'Ignored' row here rather than inventing a new color. Missing Masters' own `mmDisplayStatus`/`MM_STATUS` pattern (a status key -> {label, badgeClass} lookup) is the shape to mirror for adding this as a real distinct status alongside the existing 'missing'/'archive-missing' kinds.

SCOPE CORRECTION (director confirmed live while testing, before this even got built): this needs to cover BOTH row kinds, not just plain missing-file rows. Real live observation -- several rows showing 'archive mismatch' (the honest-messaging feature, describeArchiveMismatch) turned out to be mods that are ALSO Ignored in Vortex. So both `kind === 'missing'` AND `kind === 'archive-missing'` rows need the same Ignored check/reclassification -- an ignored mod's archive not matching shouldn't read as a real problem either, same reasoning either way.

SCOPE:
1. During scan (`lib/missing-files-scan.js`/`web/rebuild-missing-routes.js`'s scan flow), for each collection call `listIgnoredMods` once (same `isVortexRunning()` gate this route already applies elsewhere -- this is a genuinely new live Vortex-state read for this scan, gate it the same way).
2. For each row that would otherwise be `kind: 'missing'` OR `kind: 'archive-missing'`, check whether its `mod.source` matches an ignored ref via `identityKeys`. If so, mark it `kind: 'ignored'` (or an equivalent distinct field) instead -- same reclassification either way, regardless of which of the two problem kinds it would have otherwise been.
3. Table rendering: an 'Ignored' row shows the grey/soft treatment, no Extract/Download Archive action (nothing to fix, matching the acknowledged tier's own 'action buttons suppressed' convention) -- just the mod name and a plain note that it's ignored in Vortex.
4. This interacts with the just-queued filter-badges work (`rebuild-missing-filter-badges`, Missing/Archive Issue/Show all) -- check whether that item has landed yet; if so, add a third 'Ignored' badge to the same filter row rather than leaving it unfiltered; if it hasn't landed yet, still add the row-kind distinction here and note in the handoff that the badge needs a follow-up once that other item exists. Don't block on ordering, just don't silently skip either.
5. Ignored rows should NOT count toward the existing 'X missing files' summary stat/callout language (they're not actually a problem) -- check `rmfStatFiles`/`rmfStatMods`/the summary callout text and make sure an ignored mod doesn't inflate those numbers.

VERIFY live against a real collection with at least one genuinely Ignored mod that also has missing files (may need to mark one Ignored via Vortex first if none exist) -- confirm it shows the grey Ignored treatment, no action buttons, doesn't count in the missing-files stats, and (if the filter-badges item has landed) filters correctly via its own badge. Handoff with what you tested.

items.title: Rebuild Missing Files: show "Last dealt with" per collection, like Rebuild Collection's Last extracted
items.why: Director wants to see at a glance when a collection was last actually fixed via Rebuild Missing Files, matching the existing Last-extracted convention on Rebuild Collection's own picker.
items.prompt:
Director's ask: show a "Last extracted"-style timestamp for Rebuild Missing Files, same idea as Rebuild Collection's own per-collection "Last extracted: ..." label (`web/rebuild-routes.js`'s `findLastExtracted`, displayed in `web/public/app.js` ~line 197/416) -- so it's obvious, at a glance on the picker, when a collection was last actually dealt with here.

IMPORTANT DIFFERENCE FROM REBUILD COLLECTION, don't copy its mechanism wholesale: Rebuild Collection derives this from its own heavy per-run JSON log system (logsDir, findLatestRealLog, runStatus tracking, resumability) -- Rebuild Missing Files has NO equivalent persistent history at all today (confirmed via code read: extract results only ever live in-memory for the current SSE session, nothing written to disk). Don't build the full run-log machinery just for this -- a lightweight, purpose-built timestamp store is enough (e.g. a small JSON file mapping collectionModId -> last-dealt-with ISO timestamp, written directly, no resumability/halted-critical states needed since this tool has none of those concepts).

JUDGMENT CALL, flagging rather than guessing: what counts as "dealt with"? Two real options:
  (a) Only a successful FIX (at least one file actually Extracted or an archive actually Downloaded) counts -- a scan alone (just looking) doesn't update the timestamp.
  (b) Any completed scan updates it too, including a scan that found nothing wrong (confirms the user checked and it was clean).
Recommend (a) -- "dealt with" reads as "did something about it," matching Rebuild Collection's own "Last extracted" (a real rebuild happened, not just a picker load) -- but flag this choice in the handoff since it's a real product decision, not a technical one.

SCOPE:
1. On a successful Extract (`POST /extract`) or Download Archive action that actually fixes at least one file/archive for a collection, record `{collectionModId: nowISO}` to the new lightweight store.
2. Surface it on the Step 1 picker (`web/public/rebuild-missing-app.js`'s `rmfRenderPickerGroup`), same sub-line convention as this project's other 'Last X' displays (Rebuild Collection's own inline `— Last extracted: {date}`, or Workshop Report's own absolute+relative two-line format under the mod count -- pick whichever fits this card layout better and say why).
3. `GET /collections` (this router's own picker-data endpoint) needs to include this per collection.

VERIFY live: run a real Extract or Download Archive fix for a collection, confirm the picker shows the new timestamp afterward (reload the page to confirm it's actually persisted, not just an in-memory optimistic update), confirm a collection never touched here shows no timestamp at all (not a misleading blank/zero date). Handoff with what you tested and which judgment call you went with.
